title: A hand on the handle
note:
The door does not move in this one. That is the point of the rung: the sound and sight of the handle being touched, with nothing opening.

The continuity:room reference to door-cover.png was removed before the first restyle round. Every rung carried both it and the continuity:ladder reference to the rung before, and their instructions contradict each other on the one thing the ladder cannot get wrong: the ladder role says match the previous rung's camera exactly, and the room role says match door-cover's camera exactly — but door-cover is a different shot, with the door open and the guest in it. Two attachments arguing about the camera is the shape of the round-1 failure. The previous rung is the room reference, and a better one: the tan-era record shows the camera holding to four pixels across four generations when each frame was attached to the last and nothing else competed. door-stay-03-onestep keeps its door-cover reference because it is the head of the ladder and has no previous rung to use instead.

Round 22 got every content claim right and was rejected on the camera. Measured against the three rungs before it, the floor line dropped from 678 to 707, the door's top edge rose from 103 to 93 and the door widened by 24px — the camera had come down and closer, which reads as nothing on its own and as a different room in sequence. Rungs 1–3 had held the floor line to two pixels. The ladder attachment alone did not hold it here, so the framing is stated as proportions of the frame as well, the same fix that worked on door-sound-03-name-distant when placement instructions kept failing: name the measurable thing.
scene: Interior entry hall, side view, camera at standing eye level. This is the same room, the same camera position and the same distance from the viewer as the other rungs of this ladder: Lucy's rectangular cool-grey dog bed on the left, the closed charcoal front door on the right, and a clear span of taupe-grey floor between them, with the whole walk from bed to door visible in frame. Lucy lies on the bed in a settled down — elbows and hips on the bed, head up and level, watching calmly. Her size in frame, the bed's position and the camera never change between these pictures. No leash. THE CAMERA DOES NOT MOVE, and this is the rung where it drifted: keep the framing of the attached previous rung exactly. The line where the wall meets the floor runs straight across the picture at 62% of its height, so the wall fills the upper five-eighths and the floor the lower three-eighths. The door's top edge sits at 9.5% of the frame height and the door occupies from 75% to 93% of the frame width — it is a modest door across the room, not a large one close to the viewer. Do not zoom in, do not lower the camera, and do not enlarge the door because the handler is standing at it. Only one thing changes from the previous rung: the handler now stands at the closed front door with one hand resting on its handle. She stands still and relaxed, in profile to the viewer, looking at the door rather than at Lucy. The door has not moved: it is fully shut in its frame, no gap, no daylight, no shadow of an opening. Lucy holds her down on the bed across the room.
mustBeTrue: the wall-to-floor line runs across the frame at about 62% of its height and the door is the same size and in the same place as in the attached previous rung, the door is completely shut with no gap and no daylight showing, the handler's hand rests on the handle without pulling it, and Lucy holds her down on the bed.
